Subject: PO process for listing on Azure/GCP/AWS marketplaces

Hi Rafael,

We're getting ready to list some paid offerings on AWS and Azure marketplaces (and possibly GCP later this quarter). Procurement asked me to confirm Redwood's preferred PO and billing flows for marketplace listings so we can align our internal purchase orders. A few specific questions: 

- Do we send a PO to Redwood directly or to the cloud marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP)?
- For AWS, is a Private Offer required to have Redwood receive invoicing directly, or can we be billed through the marketplace?
- What billing entity should we reference on the PO (legal name, tax ID)?

Can you share the minimal intake fields your finance team needs and any forms we should complete? If it helps, happy to schedule a short call later this week.

Thanks,

Monica — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Vanessa (Finance) and Ben (Marketplace Ops) to confirm exact routing. High level:

1) Marketplace vs Direct invoicing
   - AWS: if you want Redwood to invoice you directly, the typical path is AWS Private Offer (we accept private-offer billing or we can sell via marketplace and AWS invoices CloudLane).
   - Azure: usually billed through Microsoft Marketplace (platform invoices), but we can do a reseller/partner billing arrangement on request.
   - GCP: similar to Azure; early setups typically go through the marketplace billing flow.

2) What we need from Procurement (minimal):
   - Legal entity name
   - Billing address and email for invoice delivery
   - Purchase order PDF (sample) or PO number and expected net terms
   - W9 or local tax form (if US)

3) Forms / next steps
   - Attached: vendor intake form (basic vendor + tax info) and an internal billing matrix that maps marketplace types to invoice recipients.
   - Vanessa will confirm net terms and DocuSign path if a SoF/contract is required.

If you can send the intake info and indicate preferred marketplace (AWS private offer vs marketplace listing), we can pick the right routing. If useful, I can propose a 20-min window on Wednesday.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive — Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

Hi Monica — Vanessa here from Finance. Quick checklist and clarifications so we don't miss anything: 

Required to issue invoices to you directly (per marketplace):
- AWS (Private Offer): we can accept POs and invoice CloudLane directly. Please include exact legal name + billing address + remit-to. Private Offer will also need the AWS Seller Private Offer ID once created.
- AWS (Marketplace listing): AWS often invoices the buyer; Redwood receives settlement from AWS. In that case, CloudLane would need to purchase via marketplace and pay AWS.
- Azure / GCP: typically marketplace invoicing goes through Microsoft/Google — exceptions possible but require partner/reseller setup.

Documentation we need attached to your PO submission: 
- Completed vendor intake form (attached)
- Signed SoF or purchase agreement if purchase exceeds $25k (we can route a DocuSign)
- W9 (US) or applicable VAT/tax registration

Net terms and PO routing:
- Standard: Net 30 after invoice receipt if PO specifies Net 30 (we can offer Net 45 for initial enterprise pilots with finance approval).
- Please confirm invoice email for AP and whether CloudLane requires a PO number on the invoice.

I've attached a short routing matrix (procurement_routing_matrix.csv) that maps common scenarios to our billing contacts (finance@redwood.ai or marketplace@redwood.ai). Also included is a DocuSign link to our standard SoF where applicable: https://docusign.example.com/sofs/redwood-marketplace

Next steps:
- Monica: send completed intake form + sample PO + W9
- Rafael/Ben: we'll coordinate marketplace ops to spin up the private offer or provide the marketplace listing instructions.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if you'd like to walk through it live.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
